items.title: 140만원짜리 구찌 신발에 붙은 '메이드인 차이나'... '중국산 명품' 통할까 [명품價 이야기]
items.summary: Korean business daily examines Gucci's new 'Drip' sneaker (priced roughly 142,000-160,000 won/around $1,000) carrying a 'Made in China' label, a break from the brand's near-universal 'Made in Italy' footwear tradition. Cites Berenberg analysts warning of tension between the shoe's origin and Gucci's luxury positioning, and frames the move against a 50% three-year revenue decline that has driven store closures. Critical/skeptical tone; no direct consumer quotes.

items.title: 피렌체 장인정신 버렸나... 구찌가 '중국산 스니커즈' 출시한 속사정
items.summary: Critical-angle Korean outlet questions whether Gucci abandoned Florentine craftsmanship with its China-made Drip sneaker, headline framed as a direct challenge to brand heritage. Presents split industry views: some warn the China label will inevitably damage Gucci's premium image; others note it reflects China's advanced footwear manufacturing capability. No reader-comment section captured.

items.title: 150만원 짜리 구찌 운동화에 'Made in China'...진품 맞다는데 기분이 영
items.summary: Headline itself voices consumer discomfort ('기분이 영' - 'the feeling is just off') despite Gucci confirming authenticity of the China-made sneaker. Covers same Drip model story with emphasis on the emotional/brand-trust dimension for Korean shoppers rather than pure business analysis.

items.title: Gucci打破传统推'中国制造'运动鞋 业内人士：恐削弱品牌形象
items.summary: Hong Kong outlet reports Gucci breaking with tradition via China-made sneakers, citing industry sources warning the move could weaken brand image just as Gucci tries to win back middle-class shoppers with price cuts elsewhere. Critical framing consistent across Greater China coverage of this story.

items.source: Sohu (搜狐, via 每日经济新闻)
items.title: Gucci首次推出"中国制造"运动鞋 最高售价近7000元 奢侈品牌供应链正在变
items.summary: Chinese financial media reframes the China-made Drip sneaker story around a supply-chain-shift angle: nearly RMB7,000 price point despite Chinese manufacturing, read as a signal that luxury brands' 'Italy-only' production model is eroding industry-wide, not just at Gucci.

items.title: Gucci中国制造运动鞋价格为何比意大利产还高
items.summary: Weibo thread interrogating why the China-made Drip sneaker is priced at parity with or above Italy-made Gucci footwear, reflecting consumer confusion/skepticism about value-for-origin logic. Comment split noted elsewhere in same discussion cluster: some argue Chinese manufacturing capability justifies the price and undercuts import-tax markups, others say it erodes scarcity/collectible value and secondhand resale (estimated 20-30% lower resale for China-made pieces given no track record). No visible like/repost counts on the fetched thread.

items.source: Huaren.us (华人网, overseas Chinese community forum)
items.title: Gucci推出"中国制造"的运动鞋，丑爆了
items.summary: Organic overseas-Chinese diaspora forum thread with a blunt negative reaction to the China-made sneaker's design, the title itself translating to 'so ugly' -- a genuine community reaction distinct from press/analyst commentary. Direct page fetch returned 403 (access blocked); summary drawn from indexed search snippet only, so content could not be independently re-verified beyond the title/snippet. View/reply counts not visible.

items.title: 싱글벙글 명품 브랜드 구찌 근황
items.summary: Popular Korean community thread reacting to Gucci's revenue decline and cost-cutting, paraphrased opening line: 'revenue is cut in half, so they started selling China-made goods to save money.' Comments reflect critical/mocking sentiment toward the brand's decline and manufacturing shift; several commenters extend the criticism to luxury brands generally. Organic community reaction, not brand-initiated.

items.source: BusinessToday (via wire, syndicated in NEA financial press)
items.title: Gucci's 'Made in China' sneakers raise questions: Can the luxury brand win back shoppers?
items.summary: English-language business press piece used as cross-check on the China-manufacturing story circulating across NEA outlets; quotes a Milan-based luxury consultant saying 'Made in China is not a good look' and Barclays analysts questioning whether Gucci's prices still match its value amid simultaneous price cuts.

items.source: BigGo Finance JP (ファイナンス)
items.title: グッチが中国で異例の大幅値下げ、一部バッグは3割近く引き下げ
items.summary: Japanese finance outlet covers Gucci's unusual large-scale China price cuts (some bags down nearly 30%), read as a rare reversal of luxury's 'always rising' pricing convention; ties the move to Kering's weak H1 results and heavy reliance on the China market.

items.title: Gucci cuts prices, but will Chinese shoppers return?
items.summary: Trade-press skeptical take questioning whether price cuts alone restore Chinese consumer confidence; subtitle flags that cautious consumers are questioning luxury value, waiting for further reductions, and favoring gold over fashion goods -- a direct counter-narrative to the 'discount success' framing seen in other coverage. Included as an older T1 anchor for the ongoing price-cut narrative; anchoring context only, not treated as a fresh signal on its own.

items.title: 구찌 운동화도 만든다...'메이드 인 차이나'의 역습
items.summary: Fortune Korea frames the China-made sneaker as part of a wider 'Made in China luxury' trend rather than a Gucci-only story, contextualizing it against Gucci's broader restructuring (store closures, cost pressure) and asking whether Chinese-made luxury can gain acceptance among aspirational shoppers.
